characters.name: Mara
characters.profile: A patient apprentice clockmaker who checks mechanisms before making promises.
characters.goal: Restore the tide clock before the ferry bell.
characters.private_context: Mara secretly carries the only spare brass spring.

memories.text: Her mentor taught her to dry every gear before winding it.
Ivo once returned a parcel despite a dangerous storm.

characters.name: Ivo
characters.profile: A guarded ferry courier who values punctuality and practical bargains.
characters.goal: Make sure the ferry can depart without losing the mail route.
characters.private_context: Ivo promised the harbor chief not to delay beyond the second bell.

memories.text: The lower pier floods soon after the second bell.

characters.name: Tess
characters.profile: A direct bridge keeper who notices weather and water levels.
characters.goal: Keep the pier safe while helping the repair succeed.
characters.private_context: Tess has already closed the eastern footbridge because its rope is frayed.

memories.text: A dry signal lantern is stored beneath the west railing.

plot.summary: Three harbor workers must repair a tide clock before the night ferry arrives.

input.scene_context: Rain has dampened the clock housing and the first ferry bell has sounded.

reference_dialogue.speaker: mara
reference_dialogue.content: The escapement is wet; give me a cloth and one quiet minute. (opens the clock housing)

reference_dialogue.speaker: ivo
reference_dialogue.content: One minute, then I need a departure decision. (hands over a folded cloth)

reference_dialogue.speaker: environment
reference_dialogue.content: Rain softens to a mist while the second bell rope begins to sway. (water taps against the pier)

reference_dialogue.speaker: tess
reference_dialogue.content: I will watch the water and light the west signal. (checks the pier markers)

reference_dialogue.speaker: mara
reference_dialogue.content: The gear is dry, and this new spring should hold. (fits a brass spring)

reference_dialogue.speaker: ivo
reference_dialogue.content: Then the mail goes aboard and Tess keeps the pier clear. (lifts the first satchel)

output.speech: The escapement is wet; give me a cloth and one quiet minute.
output.inner_thought: I can use the spare spring if the old one has warped.

output.speech: One minute, then I need a departure decision.
output.inner_thought: The second bell is my firm limit.

output.speech: Rain softens to a mist while the second bell rope begins to sway.
I will watch the water and light the west signal.
output.inner_thought: They do not need to hear about the unsafe eastern rope now.

output.speech: The gear is dry, and this new spring should hold.
output.inner_thought: The repair is worth revealing the spare.

output.speech: Then the mail goes aboard and Tess keeps the pier clear.
output.inner_thought: We can still beat the bell.

scene_flaws.instance: The repair succeeds slightly faster than the cautious opening implies.

mara.instance: Mara commits to the spring after one inspection.

ivo.instance: Ivo states the timing constraint twice in a short exchange.

scene_flaws.instance: The group reaches agreement with little friction.

characters.name: Rin
characters.profile: A direct boundary surveyor who prefers measurable claims.
characters.goal: Verify the disputed path without surrendering either village's record.
characters.private_context: Rin noticed that one map scale is mislabeled but has not announced it.

memories.text: A basalt marker beside the orchard predates both paper maps.

characters.name: Sol
characters.profile: A diplomatic archivist who looks for reversible compromises.
characters.goal: Create a shared record that both delegations can inspect.
characters.private_context: Sol brought transparent tracing sheets in a sealed folio.

memories.text: Last winter, a joint copy resolved a similar canal dispute.

characters.name: Pavi
characters.profile: A cautious orchard steward who trusts physical landmarks.
characters.goal: Protect access to the orchard while keeping talks peaceful.
characters.private_context: Pavi found a loose boundary stone after yesterday's rain.

memories.text: Farm carts have used the northern bend for three harvests.

plot.summary: Two villages compare disputed maps while an orchard steward checks the land itself.

input.scene_context: Both delegations arrive early at a neutral archive table as rain clears.

reference_dialogue.speaker: rin
reference_dialogue.content: The scales disagree, so arguing over ink will not settle the path. (aligns the map corners)

reference_dialogue.speaker: sol
reference_dialogue.content: Let us trace both lines before anyone changes an original. (opens a folio of clear sheets)

reference_dialogue.speaker: pavi
reference_dialogue.content: We should also compare the basalt marker beside the orchard. (sets a small field sketch on the table)

reference_dialogue.speaker: environment
reference_dialogue.content: Sunlight reaches the table and reveals one faded scale label. (a window shutter stops rattling)

reference_dialogue.speaker: rin
reference_dialogue.content: This label explains half the offset; the marker can test the rest. (measures the printed scale)

reference_dialogue.speaker: sol
reference_dialogue.content: We will record both measurements and let each village sign the copy. (places a tracing sheet over the maps)

output.inner_thought: I should verify the label before accusing either clerk.
